articles.body: Depot vs GitHub Actions hosted runners is not a price comparison: Depot charges $0.006 a minute for a 2 vCPU Linux runner, which is GitHub-hosted list price to the cent. You choose Depot for what the same money buys, which is seven times the disk, a RAM-disk accelerator and per-second metering, and you stay on GitHub-hosted if your repositories are public or your minutes fit inside the free allowance. Identical $0.006/min rates, read 20 September 2026. The difference on a 40-job matrix of 70-second jobs is rounding: 80 billed minutes against 47. GitHub-hosted runners come with the platform: nothing to install, an included monthly allowance, and a standard private-repo Linux machine of 2 vCPU, 8 GB of RAM and 14 GB of disk.

articles.excerpt: 지금 암호화폐 시장은 온통 붉은빛이다. 공포/탐욕 지수는 '극심한 공포'를 나타내는 10까지 곤두박질쳤고, 지난 24시간 동안 전체 시가총액은 약 6%나 줄어들어 2조 2,200억 달러 수준에 머물렀다. 비트코인만 해도 65,661달러까지 떨어졌으니 말이다. 이 바닥을 30년 가까이 지켜본 경험으로 보면, 투기 거품이 걷히고 나면 시장의 건전성과 불법 자금…
articles.body: 지금 암호화폐 시장은 온통 붉은빛이다. 공포/탐욕 지수는 '극심한 공포'를 나타내는 10까지 곤두박질쳤고, 지난 24시간 동안 전체 시가총액은 약 6%나 줄어들어 2조 2,200억 달러 수준에 머물렀다. 비트코인만 해도 65,661달러까지 떨어졌으니 말이다. 이 바닥을 30년 가까이 지켜본 경험으로 보면, 투기 거품이 걷히고 나면 시장의 건전성과 불법 자금 관련한 심각한 질문들이 수면 위로 떠오르기 마련이다. 지금 가장 뜨거운 감자 중 하나는 바로 AML 트래블 룰이 무한히 확장하는 '허가 없는(permissionless)' 탈중앙화 금융(DeFi) 세상에도 과연 적용될 수 있느냐는 문제다. 이 룰은 애초에 전통 금융과 중앙화된 암호화폐 거래소를 위해 설계된 것이었으니 말이다. 규제 당국이 디파이를 길들이려 할지 말지가 아니라, '어떻게' 길들일지가 관건이다. 혁신과 규제의 쫓고 쫓기는 게임을 수년간 관찰하며 다듬어 온 내 견해는 이렇다. 트래블 룰을 디파이의 핵심, 즉 진정으로 탈중앙화된 프로토콜에 직접적이고 전면적으로 적용하는 건 근본적으로 불가능하다는 거다. 대신 규제의 압력은 디파이의 '가장자리'를 중심으로 뭉칠 것이다. 디파이가 전통 금융 시스템이나 중앙화된 주체와 만나는 지점들, 그리고 가상자산 사업자(VASP)로 해석될 수 있는 특정 생태계 참여자들에게 말이다. 이는 단순히 기술적인 문제가 아니다. 감시를 위해 설계된 시스템과, 신뢰 불필요성(trustlessness) 및 익명성을 기반으로 구축된 패러다임 사이의 이념적 충돌이라고 봐야 한다. 배경 먼저 트래블 룰 자체부터 살펴보자.

articles.title: GitHub Actions Matrix must define at least one vector, and its siblings
articles.excerpt: GitHub Actions Matrix must define at least one vector is raised when a strategy has a matrix block that produced neither a dimension nor a usable include list. It is one of five distinct messages the…
articles.body: GitHub Actions Matrix must define at least one vector is raised when a strategy has a matrix block that produced neither a dimension nor a usable include list. It is one of five distinct messages the matrix converter can record, and each of the five names a different part of the block, which makes the message itself the fastest diagnosis you will get. Each message belongs to one branch of the converter. Reading which part of the block it names is faster than reading the matrix itself. What this error means The workflow is annotated and no run starts. The annotation quotes a sentence about the matrix rather than about YAML, so the file parsed correctly and was rejected one layer later, while the strategy was being turned into a list of job configurations.

articles.title: AI Agent Testing Cost: What Evals Add to Your Build Budget
articles.excerpt: AI agent testing cost usually lands between a tenth and a fifth of the total build, and that money buys three things: a labelled set of real inputs with known good outputs, a way to score the agent ag…
articles.body: AI agent testing cost usually lands between a tenth and a fifth of the total build, and that money buys three things: a labelled set of real inputs with known good outputs, a way to score the agent against them automatically, and a habit of re-running that score before every change ships. A quote with no line for this has moved the testing onto your customers, who will run it for you in production, one complaint at a time. What AI agent testing cost actually covers Testing a normal web feature means checking that a given input produces a given output, and the answer is yes or no. An agent built on a language model gives a slightly different answer every time, calls tools you did not anticipate, and degrades quietly when the model provider updates something.

articles.title: Denied requested access to the resource is denied on push
articles.excerpt: Denied requested access to the resource is denied is the registry telling you it knows exactly who you are and the answer is still no, which is why logging in again never helps. The interesting part i…
articles.body: Denied requested access to the resource is denied is the registry telling you it knows exactly who you are and the answer is still no, which is why logging in again never helps. The interesting part is that the same code covers a refusal about the image you sent, not only about the account that sent it. Three of the four are about the credential. The fourth is a policy on the registry refusing the manifest class, which sends the same code with a different message. What this error means The login step says it succeeded, layers may upload, and the push stops on a 403. The line is short and carries no detail. What Docker prints is the registry error code followed by its default message, so the word denied appears once as the code and once inside the sentence.

Tons of people are planning to take time off from work or school in order to sink their teeth into Rockstar's newest adventure. Many of them will be diving headfirst into Jason and Lucia's story, taking on high-stakes robberies to see how the couple's ascent through Vice City's underworld plays out. articles.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 236 — Alienspotting
articles.excerpt: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize.
articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.excerpt: We're scared of the Xenomorphs again, but Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 knows old-fashioned bug hunts shouldn't be a thing of the past.
articles.body: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years.

articles.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
articles.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Hele…
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely .

articles.title: Why did Starship Flight 15 booster abort 'chopsticks' landing catch? SpaceX still investigating (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13) during the Starship Flight 15 test.
articles.body: Update for 3:40 p.m. ET on Nov. 14: SpaceX's Kate Tice provided more information about the booster abort at about 3:30 p.m. EST (1830 GMT) on Nov. 14, during the company's Flight 15 webcast. "Early indications are that the booster ended its boostback [burn] early due to a low fuel mass alarm," she said. "The team is still investigating the root cause on that." SpaceX is looking into why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier.
